children: Conservative attorney John Eastman has asked the U.S. Supreme Court to reinstate his California law license after he was disbarred in the state earlier this year over his efforts to overturn Republican President Donald Trump's 2020 election loss to Democrat Joe Biden.

Eastman said in a petition to the high court filed on Friday that his legal advocacy was protected by the First Amendment of the U.S. Constitution, and that he was disciplined in a "politicized" bar proceeding. He said other attorneys who took part in legal proceedings that sought to overturn the results of the 2020 presidential election were not disciplined.

"While states may regulate genuine attorney misconduct, they may not use disciplinary authority to punish protected advocacy by relabeling it as professional misconduct," the petition said. Eastman is represented in the Supreme Court petition by Jay Sekulow, another former lawyer for Trump.

Sekulow did not immediately respond to a request for comment. It is rare for the U.S. Supreme Court to weigh in on attorney disciplinary cases, which are normally decided by the top court of respective states.

A former law professor at Chapman University in California, ​Eastman had represented Trump in a long-shot lawsuit at the U.S. Supreme Court that sought to invalidate votes in four states where the Republican former president had falsely claimed evidence of widespread voter fraud in the 2020 US presidential election.

Eastman had ​also drafted legal memos weeks after the election suggesting then-Vice President Mike Pence could ​refuse to accept electoral votes from several swing states when Congress convened to certify the vote count. ‌Pence ⁠had rebuffed his arguments, saying he did not have the legal authority to do so under the U.S. Constitution.

Eastman repeated many of his election claims at a rally outside the White House on January 6, 2021, after which a mob of Trump supporters stormed the ​U.S. Capitol and delayed ​congressional certification of the ⁠election.

A judge on California's State Bar Court had recommended Eastman's disbarment in March 2024, determining that his efforts to derail Biden's ​victory were "unlawful and lacked any factual or legal support." Eastman's law ​license was ⁠suspended as he appealed the finding.

The State Bar Court's appellate division had last year found that Eastman violated California attorney ethics rules against misleading courts and making false public statements. The California Supreme Court denied Eastman's petition for review.

Eastman had argued to the bar court's Review Department that his rights to free speech and due process were violated by state bar prosecutors, and complained that he was singled out for punishment by the judge who heard his case.
